subject: The fitted-bedroom journey from measure to installation
hook: What happens between the measure and fitting day
ig:
The part of a fitted wardrobe you never see is the part that decides how well it fits.

After we measure your bedroom, the drawings go to our workshop in Hanley. This is how we work from there:

Panels are cut on a sliding table panel saw to the sizes from your survey.
Every visible edge is sealed with ABS edging, which protects the board and keeps the finish clean.
A multi-spindle boring machine drills the hinge and shelf-pin holes, so rows line up across every section.
Carcasses are assembled and checked on the bench before they are wrapped for the van.

That last point matters: you get a wardrobe built by us, not a box of parts.

Want to see the finished side of the story? Our fitted wardrobe page is linked in bio.
fb:
Ever wondered what happens to your wardrobe between the day we measure and the day we fit it?

This is the bit in the middle. Our team in Hanley cuts every panel to the sizes taken in your room, seals the edges, drills the hinge and shelf holes on our boring machine, and assembles and checks each section on the bench.

By the time it arrives, the hard work is done, which keeps fitting day calmer for you. And no, there is no flat-pack involved at any point.

See our fitted wardrobes:
